subjects.label: Clans and champions
subjects.description: Which clan or champion a player runs, how the clans differ from one another, which is strongest or weakest and wants a buff, random clan selection, and wanting more of them; not general remarks that the game is a deckbuilder.

subjects.label: Builds and card keywords
subjects.description: A named build or card keyword a run is put together around, such as frostbite, multistrike, thorns stacking or kill triggers, and whether it carries a run; not which clan was picked in itself.

subjects.label: Covenant ranks and unlock progression
subjects.description: The ladder of covenant difficulty ranks opened after a win and the clan levels and card unlocks that persist between runs, including their being lost or blocked; not a one-off complaint that a fight is too hard.

subjects.label: One more run
subjects.description: The pull to start another run straight after the last one, staying up past midnight, sinking twenty hours in two days and being unable to put it down; not a plain statement that the game is fun.

subjects.label: Train premise and puns
subjects.description: The game being set on a train and the jokes that invites: choo choo, all aboard, driving the train, passengers on board, a train-shaped take on tower climbing; not the story told along the way.

subjects.label: Bosses and the enemy roster
subjects.description: The angels, seraphs and named bosses that board the train, what particular enemies do, and how hard the late waves and bosses hit; not the player's own units or decks.

subjects.label: Streamers and videos
subjects.description: Coming to the game because a streamer or YouTuber played it, or telling others to watch videos of it before judging; not the reviewer's own verdict on the game.

subjects.label: Run length
subjects.description: How long a single run takes, whether runs or the game feel short, and whether a short run makes it easier to go again; not how many hours the game lasts overall or how much content there is.
